app.title: FLIM Playground – Data Analysis
app.summary: A person uploads a table of per-cell measurements, checks how its columns were read (row ID, categorical metadata, measurement groups), and picks a univariate, bivariate or multivariate module. They narrow the rows with categorical and numeric filters, then encode categories by colour, shape, opacity or separate panels, and can average replicates into one point per group. Each module computes something specific: group comparisons with effect sizes and t-tests, histograms or 2D distributions with Gaussian mixture subpopulations, phasor plots, PCA/UMAP/t-SNE embeddings, or a trained classifier with ROC and confusion matrix. They leave with the figure, a CSV of the subpopulation each row was assigned to, and a standalone Python script that reproduces the whole analysis.

task.text: Compare per-cell measurements across experimental groups, find subpopulations and separate conditions, and export a reproducible analysis.

data.text: A table of measurements per item, with categorical metadata columns (condition, replicate, image) and numeric feature columns organised into named groups, such as per-channel lifetime, intensity and phasor features.
data.item: a single cell segmented from an image, with its metadata and measured features

stage.text: analysing extracted single-cell features and comparing conditions, after image extraction

mechanism.text: A left column picks the module, features and model settings; the right column holds filters, encoding channels, the plot and its styling, so every module shares the same filter and grouping controls. Plots split by a category show an overview grid where clicking a panel promotes it to the large view, and fitted subpopulations can be named and exported alongside a generated script that reproduces the figure.

field.text: single-cell feature analysis of fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLIM) in cell biology

workflow.name: compare groups of measured items across features and export a reproducible analysis

steps.here: Upload a CSV, TSV, Excel or ODS table; a review gate shows the detected column roles and feature groups, which can be edited, applied to this upload or saved as a reusable profile before any plot appears.

steps.step: choose the analysis and the features it uses
steps.here: Radio buttons pick Univariate, Bivariate or Multivariate, then a module (Feature Comparison, Feature Histogram, 2D Feature Distribution, Phasor Plot, Dimension Reduction, Classification); grouped feature selectors pick one, two or many features, with module settings such as effect size, t-test, UMAP/t-SNE hyperparameters or classifier and train split.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Categorical columns become include/exclude multiselects and numeric conditions (feature, operator, threshold) can be chained; rows missing the selected features are dropped.
Colour, shape, opacity, subcolour and separate-by channels map categorical columns onto the plot; collapse-by averages replicates (e.g. per patient) into one point per group.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Each module computes its result: Glass's delta or Cohen's d and t-tests between groups, Gaussian mixture subpopulations chosen by BIC, regression and marginals, phasor coordinates, PCA/UMAP/t-SNE embeddings, or classifier metrics with ROC and confusion matrix.
A plot split by a category shows every level as a small panel; clicking one promotes it to the large view, and the x-axis order of groups can be dragged.
Name the fitted mixture components and download a CSV of each row's subpopulation, then download a standalone Python script that reproduces the filters, encodings, fits and figure.

distinctive: Columns are sorted into three roles (row ID, categorical metadata, grouped numeric features) and every control is driven by those roles, so filters come from categories and selectors from feature groups.
Collapse-by averages replicate measurements within each group, so statistics compare biological replicates instead of individual cells.
A phasor plot of lifetime G/S coordinates per channel and harmonic appears only when the table holds phasor features.
Gaussian mixture components found in a histogram or 2D distribution can be named and written back as a per-cell subpopulation column.
The whole on-screen analysis, including filters and styling, is exported as an editable Python script that redraws the figure.
